title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E526 treats transverse vibrations of an elastic rod or lamina. The governing equation is in effect the Euler–Bernoulli beam equation, with Euler's constants b, c and his convention that g is the fall-height in one second, so gravitational acceleration is 2g. On the previous page Euler separates variables. He seeks 'regular' vibrations y = M(s)·sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)), that is, motion synchronous with a simple pendulum of length k. This reduces the spatial equation to M'''' = M/f⁴ with f = (bcck)^{1/4}. Its general solution is y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k))·(α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f)).

This page:
(1) Euler finishes the pendulum analogy. The time of one vibration, meaning a half-period in Euler's counting, is π√(k/2g) seconds. The number of vibrations per second is √(2g)/(π√k), which serves as the measure of the pitch.
(2) Corollary 1 (§10): he expands the four spatial functions in power series in x = s/f and collects terms. The result is S = (α+β+δ) + (α−β+γ)x + (α+β−δ)x²/2! + (α−β−γ)x³/3! + …, with the coefficient pattern repeating with period 4. He remarks that the series converge the faster, the larger f is compared with the arc s, and recalls that f = (bcck)^{1/4} contains the pendulum length k.
(3) Corollary 2 (§11) begins: the s-derivatives of y are to be obtained by differentiation; they are listed on the next page.

Purpose: to set up the eigenfunctions, whose four constants will later be fixed by the end conditions, giving the transcendental frequency equations.
errors: Printing slip in the α-series: the cubic term is printed with denominator 1.2.3ff instead of 1.2.3f³.
'Eo magis convergent' is loose. The entire series converge for every s; what increases with f/s is the speed of convergence, which is clearly Euler's meaning.
Not an error, but a convention to note: the 'time of one vibration' π√(k/2g) is a half-period, with g the one-second fall height (acceleration 2g). Within these conventions both formulas are correct.

ideas.what: Separated (standing-wave) solution of the beam equation with time factor sin(ζ+ωt), ω=√(2g/k), and spatial eigenfunction a combination of e^{±s/f}, sin(s/f), cos(s/f)

ideas.what: Characterising the vibration by the equivalent simple pendulum length k; frequency √(2g)/(π√k) as the measure of pitch
ideas.modern_name: Natural frequency via equivalent pendulum length
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli; standard 18th-century practice
ideas.where_published: E65 and Euler's various papers on vibrating strings and rods

ideas.what: Power-series expansion of α e^x + β e^{-x} + γ sin x + δ cos x, with coefficients periodic of period 4
ideas.modern_name: Taylor series of the general solution of y''''=y (period-4 coefficient pattern)
ideas.where_published: E101 Introductio in analysin infinitorum (series); E65 for the beam functions

deep.surprise_reason: Routine textbook material: the pendulum-length frequency formula and a trivial series expansion of the beam eigenfunctions. Both are standard in Euler's earlier work and well documented.
transcription_corrections: In the α-line the image prints the cubic term as s³/(1.2.3ff), a typographical slip for f³; the transcription silently corrected it to f³.
The time factor in all displayed formulas is sin.(ζ + t√(2g/k)); the transcription renders this correctly.
